A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Spotlight and support reliable comparison. All 30 pages of v1 and 31 pages of v2, including Appendices A–F, are readable; figures, tables, equations, and relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original results from three synthetic benchmarks, prompting experiments, demonstration studies, and a user study with 50 recruited participants.

after.justification: V2 retains these original benchmark, generated-text analysis, and user-study results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The Spotlight workflow, pattern-discovery adaptations, and selection of Premise for subsequent analyses remain unchanged. Section 4 and Appendix A describe the same procedures; switching pattern delimiters to braces is a notation edit.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three synthetic benchmarks, opinion prompts and personas, story-generation and summarization scenarios, English/German prompt comparison, and user-study population. No evaluated task or scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmark comparisons retain c-tf-idf, Premise, SPuManTE, PySubgroup, Cortana, Llama 3.1 8B/70B, and GPT-4o, with the same experiment-specific exclusions and truncated-text variants. The added related-work citations are not new evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Benchmark generation, sample sizes, metrics, and testing procedures are retained. V2's expanded Section 8 repeats settings already documented in v1 Appendix E, including the seven-person pilot, 30-word instruction, ten texts per group, randomization, and three exclusions from 50 participants.

E4.justification: The bias-strength, group-size, pattern-length, and frequency analyses are retained, alongside the same demonstration cases and user-study error analyses. Moving benchmark pattern examples and frequency-dependent recall into the main text does not add an analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same benchmark mean/standard-deviation error bars and user-study variability. Appendix E retains the same one-tailed two-proportion z-tests and Mann–Whitney U tests. Seed and repetition reporting does not change.

E6.justification: Matched tables and plots retain their results, including Premise's Benchmark 2 F1 of 0.37 and soft precision/recall of 0.9/0.7. The redesigned user-study plot preserves its bar proportions. V2's 47%/42% participant-background summaries restate data already shown in v1 Appendix E and Figure 7.

T1.justification: The token-pattern definition, synthetic transformation construction, and strict/soft matching definitions remain unchanged. Braces replace parentheses in examples without altering the mathematics; no theorem, proof, or derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about Spotlight, three benchmarks, fine-grained discoveries, and support for human evaluators. The revised conclusion makes applicability qualifications more explicit without redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: V2's Limitations explicitly identifies untested topics, information density, and sequence order, and explains why token replacement and mining may miss non-token differences. It also identifies unevaluated temperature changes and more specific user-study generalization limits concerning participant expertise, text length, and the full prompt-engineering process.

D1.justification: The main-text access statement changes from a promised future release to reporting that code, data, benchmarks, and token-pattern results are publicly available at the same repository. Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and runtime information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.4 adds Li et al.'s 2024 NLG-evaluation survey and Xu et al.'s 2023 INSTRUCTSCORE paper. This modestly expands the LLM-evaluation discussion while retaining the overall research positioning. Wu and Aji's publication update refers to the same existing work.

P1.justification: V2 expands the main-text user-study explanation, refines the discussion and limitations, and makes scattered language and terminology edits. Pattern examples largely switch to set braces, and the author/affiliation block adds Jonas Fischer. The overall section structure remains intact.

P2.justification: V1 Appendix Table 6 and Figure 5 become v2 main-text Table 2 and Figure 2. The user-study plot is enlarged, recolored, and given hatching; appendix figures and tables reflow, including placing survey Figures 7–8 together. These are limited presentation changes with retained evidence.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the existing evidence easier to assess by bringing benchmark displays and user-study details into the main text. Its more specific limitations clarify what the benchmarks and user study establish, and it reports public resource availability. These improve clarity and transparency, while the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
